study_name: Comparison of Pediatric Sequential Organ Failure Assessment and Pediatric Risk of Mortality III Score as Mortality Prediction in Pediatric Intensive Care Unit
population: Critically ill children of age one month to 15 years staying in PICU for more than 24 hours
outcome: Mortality within 30 days of PICU admitted children
performance: p-SOFA score (AUC=0.81, 95% CI=0.76-0.86, p=0.001), PRISM III 24 score (AUC=0.75, 95% CI=0.69-0.81, p=0.001). For the prediction of 30-day mortality at the cut-off value of p-SOFA>2, the sensitivity was 93.87%, specificity was 38.21%, and accuracy was 69.93%. Whereas at the cut-off value of PRISM III 24 score>8, the sensitivity was 55.83%, specificity was 77.24%, and accuracy was 65.03%
adjustment: Not reported

study_name: Besen et al.
population: Patients admitted to a Brazilian public ICU with sepsis
predictor: Sepsis-3 definitions (infection, sepsis and septic shock); Lactate levels
performance: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC); continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI); integrated discrimination index (IDI)
adjustment: Age, severity at baseline (SAPS 3), use of support measures (renal replacement therapy, mechanical ventilation)

study_name: Mortality predictors in patients with suspected sepsis in the emergency department of a tertiary care hospital
population: Adult patients with suspicion of sepsis at the ED of a tertiary care hospital in Brazil
effect_size: Positive blood cultures (RR, 1.63;95% CI, 1.10 to 2.41) and general administration of vasopressors at the ED (RR, 2.14;95% CI, 1.44 to 3.17) were associated with 30-day mortality. The administration of vasopressors at the ED (RR, 2.25; CI 95%, 1.58 to 3.21) was found to be a predictor of overall mortality.
adjustment: sex, age, different qSOFA points, different severity criteria points, time to ATB, lactate, blood cultures, creatinine, platelets, and administration of vasopressor

study_name: Epidemiology and Mortality of Sepsis in Intensive Care Units in Prefecture-Level Cities in Sichuan, China: A Prospective Multicenter Study
population: Patients admitted to the ICU of 7 tertiary hospitals in Sichuan, China between October 10, 2017 and January 9, 2018 and screened for sepsis using the Sepsis-3 criteria
predictor: central nervous system dysfunction, lowest blood phosphorus level, highest lactate level, 24-h Acute Physiologic Assessment and Chronic Health Evaluation-II (APACHE-II) score, and lung infection
effect_size: central nervous system dysfunction (odds ratio [OR]=2.59, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.15-5.84, P=0.022), lowest blood phosphorus level (OR=2.56, 95% CI: 1.21-5.44, P=0.014), highest lactate level (OR=1.20, 95% CI: 1.10-1.32, P<0.001), 24-h Acute Physiologic Assessment and Chronic Health Evaluation-II (APACHE-II) score (OR=1.08, 95% CI: 1.03-1.13, P=0.002), and lung infection (OR=2.57, 95% CI: 1.30-5.09, P=0.007)
adjustment: Variables with P<0.05 were analyzed by multivariable logistic regression using the forward method

predictor: pediatric Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score

adjustment: age, sex, admission year, and admission ward
validation_method: Receiver operating characteristic curves, DeLong’s test, integrated discrimination improvement index
